problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained differentiable objectives on a real separable Hilbert space, permitting nonconvexity, with L-Lipschitz gradients and f(x0)−inf f≤Δ. Parameters satisfy L>0 and Δ≥0; attainment of the infimum is unnecessary.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HolderNoiseNonconvex.lean: Params; spec.valid; spec.admissible gradient and initial-gap conditions.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: One call at a chosen pair (x,y) returns (g(x,ω),g(y,ω)) using the same sample. Samples are IID across calls, and E[g(x,ω)]=∇f(x). Each paired reply counts as one oracle call. All Params, including L,M,ν,σ,Δ,ε,x0, are public; f,g and the sampling laws are hidden.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HolderNoiseNonconvex.lean: spec.Public, publicInput, Query, Reply and admissible; LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: IID; LongTails/Template.lean: executeWithTrace and Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: gradient_similarity
distinctive_assumptions.details: Centered noise differences satisfy E‖(g(x,ω)−g(y,ω))−(∇f(x)−∇f(y))‖²≤M‖x−y‖^(2ν), where M≥0 and 0<ν≤1. This controls shared-sample noise increments separately from objective smoothness.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HolderNoiseNonconvex.lean: spec.valid and final two conditions of spec.admissible.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Uniform finite variance E‖g(x,ω)−∇f(x)‖²≤σ², with σ≥0. No higher-moment or exponential-tail bound is imposed.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HolderNoiseNonconvex.lean: spec.valid and spec.admissible variance integrability and bound.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is a complete real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure and second-countable topology; finite dimension is not required.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HolderNoiseNonconvex.lean: Params.normedE, innerE, completeE, measurableE, borelE and countableE.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: Return an E-valued measurable output X with integrable gradient norm and E‖∇f(X)‖≤ε, where ε>0. The criterion uses the unsquared norm.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: Expectation is over the algorithm's randomness and the IID oracle stream, under a fixed oracle-call budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The standard smooth nonconvex stationarity problem is augmented with shared-sample paired queries and a separate mean-square Hölder condition on centered noise increments throughout 0<ν≤1.

descriptionHtml:
Nonconvex Optimization with Hölder Noise

We consider minimizing a differentiable, possibly nonconvex function f:E→R on a separable real Hilbert space E. Its gradient is L-Lipschitz, with L>0, and a given point x0∈E satisfies f(x0)−infx∈Ef(x)≤Δ, with Δ≥0. Each oracle call returns unbiased gradients at two queried points using one shared sample, with independent samples across calls. The centered noise has variance at most σ2 and mean-square Hölder increments bounded by M∥x−y∥2ν, where σ,M≥0 and 0<ν≤1. The goal is a measurable output x¯∈E satisfying E∥∇f(x¯)∥≤ε, where ε>0 and expectation includes sampling and algorithm randomness.

The optimization problem is infx∈Ef(x), where ∥⋅∥ is the norm induced by the inner product on E. The algorithm receives E, the measurable sample space Ω, L, M, ν, σ, Δ, ε, and x0.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Smoothness and initial gap). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere, and for every x,y∈E, ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,f(x0)−f(x)≤Δ.

Assumption 2 (Unbiased stochastic gradients). There exist a probability measure p on Ω and a jointly measurable map g:E×Ω→E. For every x∈E, the random vector g(x,ξ) is Bochner integrable and ∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2 is integrable under ξ∼p, with Eξ∼p[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),Eξ∼p[∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2]≤σ2.

Assumption 3 (Hölder noise increments). Define the centered noise by ζ(x,ξ)=g(x,ξ)−∇f(x). For every x,y∈E, the squared increment ∥ζ(x,ξ)−ζ(y,ξ)∥2 is integrable under ξ∼p and satisfies Eξ∼p[∥ζ(x,ξ)−ζ(y,ξ)∥2]≤M∥x−y∥2ν.

At call k, a query (xk,yk)∈E×E receives (g(xk,ξk),g(yk,ξk)). The sample sequence (ξk)k≥0 consists of measurable, mutually independent random variables with common law p. Algorithm randomness is independent of the entire sample sequence. Queries may depend on earlier replies, and each paired reply counts as one oracle call.

After the allotted calls, the output x¯ must be measurable, its gradient norm must be integrable, and EP[∥∇f(x¯)∥]≤ε, where P is the joint law of the sample sequence and the algorithm’s randomness.

comparisonHtml:
On a separable real Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure, f is differentiable with L-Lipschitz gradient and f(x0)−f(x)≤Δ for every x. Here L,ε>0, M,σ,Δ≥0, and 0<ν≤1. The jointly measurable oracle g uses IID samples with law p, satisfies ∫g(x,ω)dp(ω)=∇f(x), and, with e(x,ω)=g(x,ω)−∇f(x), satisfies ∫∥e(x,ω)∥2dp(ω)≤σ2 and ∫∥e(x,ω)−e(y,ω)∥2dp(ω)≤M∥x−y∥2ν, with the stated integrands integrable. One call returns gradients at two points using one shared sample. Target: a measurable output with integrable gradient norm and ∫∥∇f(xout(ω))∥dP(ω)≤ε, where P is the sampling law. The setup imposes no algorithm restriction.

At L=M=σ=Δ=1: O(ε−4) becomes O(ε−7/2ℓ2) for ν=1/4, or O(ε−3ℓ2) for ν≥1/2, as ε→0. (1) needs centered Hölder regularity and paired same-sample access; guarantees expected norm rather than the stronger squared-norm criterion.
(3) NSGD-MVR (Fradin et al. 2026), Thm. 4.2, p=q=2; ν=1, E=Rd O(1+σ2+(L+M)Δε2+MΔσε3); paired calls including initialization (1): Scope extends the distance exponent from ν=1 to 0<ν<1; at ν=1, polynomial orders match up to logarithms. (1) incurs an ℓ2 overhead at ν=1.
(4) (LongTails 2026); raw Hölder increments, 1/2≤ν≤1 O(ℓ2[1+LΔ+σ2ε2+ΔM1/(2ν)σ2−1/νε3]) (1): Scope extends to centered noise and 0<ν<1/2, admitting quadratic means. On the common class, no worse order; cheaper when the SGD cap wins.

Abbr: ℓ=1+log⁡(2+LΔ/ε2); ρ=σ2L2ν/(Mε2ν) for M,σ>0; a=min{1,1/(2ν)}. L: population smoothness; Δ: initial gap bound; σ2: noise variance bound; (M,ν): centered-noise regularity; ε: stationarity tolerance. For σ=0, use the first branch of (1). Raw increments in (4) mean ∫∥g(x,ω)−g(y,ω)∥2dp(ω)≤M∥x−y∥2ν. Paired and single-point call counts differ by at most a universal factor on their common oracle model; batches are included. All displayed costs are sufficient budgets.

import LongTails.Template
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.MeasurableSpace
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Real

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.HolderNoiseNonconvex

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  [countableE : SecondCountableTopology E]
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  L : ℝ
  M : ℝ
  ν : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.innerE Params.completeE Params.measurableE
  Params.borelE Params.countableE Params.measurableΩ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E × p.E
  Reply p := p.E × p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.M ∧ 0 < q.ν ∧ q.ν ≤ 1 ∧ 0 ≤ q.σ ∧ 0 ≤ q.Δ ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (g : q.E → q.Ω → q.E) (p : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ω)),
      LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID
        (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ω) => ξ k) (p : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
      O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
            law := P
            answer := fun _ (_, z) ω => (g z.1 ω, g z.2 ω) } ∧
      (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
      (∀ x y, ‖gradient f x - gradient f y‖ ≤ q.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
      (∀ x, f q.x0 - f x ≤ q.Δ) ∧
      Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧
      (∀ x, Integrable (g x) p) ∧
      (∀ x, ∫ ω, g x ω ∂p = gradient f x) ∧
      (∀ x, Integrable (fun ω => ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ 2) p) ∧
      (∀ x, ∫ ω, ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ 2 ∂p ≤ q.σ ^ 2) ∧
      (∀ x y, Integrable (fun ω => ‖(g x ω - g y ω) - (gradient f x - gradient f y)‖ ^ 2) p) ∧
      (∀ x y, ∫ ω, ‖(g x ω - g y ω) - (gradient f x - gradient f y)‖ ^ 2 ∂p ≤ q.M * ‖x - y‖ ^ (2 * q.ν))
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => ‖gradient f (output ω)‖) (P : Measure _) ∧
      ∫ ω, ‖gradient f (output ω)‖ ∂(P : Measure _) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.HolderNoiseNonconvex
